texts.label: text
texts.orig: Abstract. We review twelve months of environmental swabs from a dry-blend powder line. Zone 1 contact surfaces stayed below action limits in every month, while Zone 3 floor drains drove most presumptive positives. Sanitation after wet cleaning, not the blend recipe, explained the seasonal peak. We propose a risk-weighted sampling rotation and report the effect of the change on detection rates.
texts.text: Abstract. We review twelve months of environmental swabs from a dry-blend powder line. Zone 1 contact surfaces stayed below action limits in every month, while Zone 3 floor drains drove most presumptive positives. Sanitation after wet cleaning, not the blend recipe, explained the seasonal peak. We propose a risk-weighted sampling rotation and report the effect of the change on detection rates.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Dry powder facilities depend on keeping water out. When water enters during a wet clean, organisms that persist in dry niches can grow, and a single harborage site can seed a whole zone? Environmental monitoring (EM) programs therefore sample by zone, from product-contact surfaces (Zone 1) outward to non-production areas (Zone 4).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Across 1,284 swabs, 41 were presumptive positive and 17 confirmed. Zone 3 drains accounted for 11 of the 17 confirmed results. No Zone 1 site was confirmed positive. The monthly pattern (Figure 1) peaks in March and August, the two months with the most wet cleans.
texts.text: Across 1,284 swabs, 41 were presumptive positive and 17 confirmed. Zone 3 drains accounted for 11 of the 17 confirmed results. No Zone 1 site was confirmed positive. The monthly pattern (Figure 1) peaks in March and August, the two months with the most wet cleans.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Confirmed positives followed a wet clean within seven days in 13 of 17 cases (76%). A post-clean dry-out step, added in May, reduced that share to 2 of 6 in the second half of the year.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The data point to water, not the blend recipe, as the driver. Drains and the floor around them stay wet for hours after a clean, and traffic carries that water toward Zone 2. The dry-out step shortened that window. A risk-weighted rotation puts more swabs where water lingers without adding total samples.
